title: Ala. Code § 7-2-314 — Implied warranty: merchantability; usage of trade
content:
Ala. Code § 7-2-314

(1) Unless excluded or modified (Section 7-2-316), a warranty that the goods shall be merchantable is implied in a contract for their sale if the seller is a merchant with respect to goods of that kind. Under this section the serving for value of food or drink to be consumed either on the premises or elsewhere is a sale.

(2) Goods to be merchantable must be at least such as

(a) Pass without objection in the trade under the contract description; and

(c) Are fit for the ordinary purposes for which such goods are used;

sections.content: Unless excluded or modified, a warranty that the goods shall be merchantable is implied in a contract for their sale if the seller is a merchant with respect to goods of that kind.

title: Ala. Code § 25-4-78 — Disqualification for benefits
content:
Ala. Code § 25-4-78

An individual shall be disqualified for total or partial unemployment:

(1) If he left his most recent bona fide work voluntarily without good cause connected with such work.

(2) If he was discharged or removed from his work for a dishonest or criminal act committed in connection with his work or for sabotage or an act endangering the safety of others or for the use of illegal drugs after previous warning or for the refusal to submit to or cooperate with a drug test.

sections.content: An individual shall be disqualified for total or partial unemployment if he left his most recent bona fide work voluntarily without good cause connected with such work, or if discharged for specified misconduct including dishonest or criminal acts connected with work.

title: Alaska Stat. § 23.10.060 — Payment of wages
content:

(a) An employer shall pay all wages due to an employee at least once a month, or on regular paydays designated in advance by the employer, and the paydays may not be more than 30 days apart.

(b) An employer who terminates an employee shall pay the employee all wages due within three working days after the termination.

title: Ark. Code Ann. § 11-4-210 — Minimum wage
content:

(a) Beginning October 1, 2006, every employer shall pay each of his or her employees wages at a rate of not less than six dollars and twenty-five cents ($6.25) per hour except as otherwise provided in this subchapter.

(b) Beginning January 1, 2019, every employer shall pay each of his or her employees wages at a rate of not less than nine dollars and twenty-five cents ($9.25) per hour, increasing annually thereafter as provided by law.

title: Idaho Code § 45-601 — Definitions — Wage claims
content:
Idaho Code § 45-601

As used in this chapter:

(1) "Wages" means compensation for labor or services rendered by an employee, whether the amount is determined on a time, task, piece or commission basis.

(2) "Employer" includes every person, firm, partnership, association, corporation, receiver or other officer of a court of this state, and any agent or officer of any of the above mentioned classes, employing any person in this state.

sections.content: As used in this chapter, "wages" means compensation for labor or services rendered by an employee, whether the amount is determined on a time, task, piece or commission basis.

title: Ind. Code § 22-2-5-1 — Payment of employees; frequency; exemptions

title: Iowa Code § 91A.3 — Mode of payment
content:

title: La. Rev. Stat. § 23:631 — Termination of employment; payment of wages
content:

title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 28-14-2 — Payment of wages — Frequency
content:
R.I. Gen. Laws § 28-14-2

Every employee shall be paid wages weekly, biweekly, or semimonthly, and the wages shall be paid in full. Weekly, biweekly, or semimonthly payments of wages shall be made within nine (9) days of the end of the payroll period for which the wages are due.

sections.content: Every employee shall be paid wages weekly, biweekly, or semimonthly, and the wages shall be paid in full within nine days of the end of the payroll period for which the wages are due.

title: S.C. Code Ann. § 41-10-30 — Payment of wages; notice of wages and deductions
content:
S.C. Code Ann. § 41-10-30

(A) Every employer shall notify each employee in writing at the time of hiring of the wages agreed upon and the time and place of payment. Every employer shall pay all wages due in lawful United States currency or by negotiable check or draft drawn on a financial institution insured by an agency of the federal or state government.

title: Tenn. Code Ann. § 50-2-103 — Payment of employees — Regular paydays
content:
Tenn. Code Ann. § 50-2-103

(a) All wages or other compensation for labor or services of employees in private employment shall be due and payable at least once per month. Notice of the regular payday shall be posted by each employer in at least two (2) conspicuous places where such notices can be seen by the employees as they go to and from work.

title: Utah Code § 34-28-3 — Regular paydays — Currency or negotiable instruments
content:
Utah Code § 34-28-3

(1) An employer shall pay the wages earned by an employee at regular intervals, but in periods no longer than semimonthly on days to be designated in advance by the employer as the regular payday.

(2) An employer shall pay for services rendered during a pay period within 10 days after the close of that pay period.

title: Vt. Stat. Ann. tit. 21, § 342 — Weekly payment of wages
content:
Vt. Stat. Ann. tit. 21, § 342

(a) Any employer having five or more employees shall pay weekly each employee engaged in the employer's business the wages earned by the employee to a day not more than six days prior to the date of payment. An employer may pay biweekly or semimonthly if the employer provides notice of the pay schedule to the employee.

title: D.C. Code § 32-1302 — When wages must be paid; payment of wages on discharge
content:
D.C. Code § 32-1302

An employer shall pay all wages earned by an employee at least twice during each calendar month, on regular paydays designated in advance by the employer. The end of any pay period for which payment is made on a regular payday shall not be more than 10 working days before such regular payday.
